title: The Negus Shelters the Muslim Refugees
text:
Around 615, the early followers of Muhammad in Mecca were being persecuted by the leaders of the Quraysh. Muhammad advised some of them to flee across the Red Sea to the Christian kingdom of Aksum, whose king, the Negus, called al-Najashi in Arabic, was known as a just ruler. A small group, including the Prophet's cousin Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, made the crossing.

According to Ibn Ishaq's biography of the Prophet, the Quraysh sent two envoys, one of them Amr ibn al-As, with rich gifts of leather for the king and his generals. They asked him to hand over the refugees, saying they had abandoned their people's religion without adopting his.

The Negus refused to give anyone up without hearing them. He called the Muslims before him and his bishops. Ja'far spoke for them, describing how they had lived before and what their new faith taught, and at the king's request he recited a passage from the Quran about Mary and the birth of Jesus. The Negus wept until his beard was wet. He said that this and what Jesus had brought came from the same source. He returned the gifts and told the refugees they could live safely in his land.
lesson: Give people a fair hearing before you judge them, especially when powerful voices demand that you turn them away. Justice begins with listening.
people: Al-Najashi (Ashama or Armah), Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, Amr ibn al-As
source: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah, as edited by Ibn Hisham
caveat: The account is traditional, written down more than a century later, and the king's exact identity is uncertain.
